open_points.subject: Model M01 — ObjectConnection.invoice_subfolder
open_points.text: Both subfolders are written as paths inside the root.
open_points.question: Does an invoice_subfolder that is lexically inside root but resolves through a link outside root remain a valid confirmed connection, or must its resolved target also stay inside root as is expressly required for photo_subfolder when used?
options: Only lexical containment is required for invoice_subfolder; the resolved-link check applies only to photo_subfolder when used.
Both subfolders must also resolve inside root, so an externally linked invoice folder is refused.
The invoice folder is accepted at connection time but refused only when a later invoice-reading action uses it.
open_points.default_guess: Require lexical containment for both subfolder values and resolved containment only for photo_subfolder when it is used, because that is the only linked-folder refusal stated by the product text.

witness.initial: The Registry has issued a project id; root is /srv/object, photo_subfolder names an ordinary directory inside it, and invoice_subfolder names /srv/object/invoices, which is a symbolic link to a directory outside /srv/object.
events: The owner confirms the object and those exact folders.
The agent attempts to write the confirmed ObjectConnection.
outcomes: The agent writes a confirmed connection because both stored subfolder paths are lexically inside root and only a linked photo folder has an explicit resolved-containment rule.
The agent refuses the connection because the statement about both subfolders being inside root is read as requiring their resolved targets to remain inside root.
witness.observer: The owner and agent see whether the connection is created and confirmed.
